subject: drama
topicName: Set Text Analysis and Exam Preparation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Know the WHOLE play, not just the extracts — context matters for every question.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Extract questions: analyse the specific scene AND connect it to the whole play's themes and structure.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Three perspectives: you may be asked from performer, director or designer viewpoint — always answer from the specified perspective.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Structure your answer: point (identify technique/choice) + evidence (specific reference) + explanation (effect on audience) + link (to whole play themes).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: How would you approach a written exam question asking you to describe how you would perform an extract from your set text? | Why is it important to understand the whole play, even though the exam only asks about extracts? | Describe how you would answer a question from a director's perspective about staging a key scene.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Read the extract carefully; identify the key dramatic moment; choose a perspective (performer/director/designer as asked); make specific staging/performance choices; justify each with reference to the | Extracts are shaped by the whole play — character motivations come from earlier scenes, themes run throughout, the extract's significance depends on its place in the overall structure. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the question TWICE — check which perspective is required Always refer to SPECIFIC moments in the extract — never write generically Link extract choices to the WHOLE play — context marks are essential Use PEEL paragraphs: Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link
